text:
Elena Moreno: Heads-up: scheduling maintenance for az4 GPU pool (az4-gpu-main, ~52 GPUs) next Wed 01:30-03:00 UTC. Purpose: NIC microcode + BGP preflight and staggered node reboots.
Theo Briggs: Ack. Is this going to be full node evacs or soft drains?
Elena Moreno: Soft drains in 4-node cohorts. We'll cordon -> drain -> run nvlink & PCIe sanity -> uncordon. Plan cohorts every 7 minutes to keep overlap small.
Mina Shah: If we shift traffic to us-west2 as fallback, egress could spike. Can we cap cross-az failover at 15%?
SRE-Liam: Yes, set routing policy to gradual failover with a 2-minute ramp per cohort and a hard cap at 15% cross-az. Also, enable KV cache pre-seed on backfill nodes to reduce token churn.
Theo Briggs: How long do we expect each cohort to be offline? 4-node cohort ~= 10m including sanity checks?
Elena Moreno: Target ~9min per cohort. Full run ~63min plus 15m buffer = fits 01:30-03:00.
Mina Shah: Canary procedure? We should validate microcode on 2 canary nodes before batch.
SRE-Liam: Canary set: 2 nodes isolated, run perf-suite and an inference smoke test (100 sample prompts). If any NVLINK CRC or PCIe MCEs show up, abort.
Elena Moreno: Ops checklist draft below. Add items if I missed anything:
- post tenant comms (24h & 1h reminders)
- canary validation ready
- oncall + backup assigned
- traffic cap and routing policy configured
- finance notified for burst capacity
- telemetry alerts adjusted for expected transient errors
Theo Briggs: Finance note: projecting additional GPU-hours ~26h if we run fallback on burst pool. At $3.25/hr that's ~$84.50. Approve?
Mina Shah: Approve. Add a tag so finance can bill to "infra-maint-2026Q1".
SRE-Liam: Who's oncall that slot? @infra-bot please post.
infra-bot: Scheduled oncall: Primary - SRE-Liam, Backup - Theo Briggs for 2026-03-25 01:30 UTC maintenance window.
Elena Moreno: Quick capacity sim please (fairness policy applied). If queued > 250 units we shift to regional failover.
Theo Briggs: Running sim now will paste results.
Theo Briggs: Sim result: peak queued 176 units, projected GPU util 91% during cohort 5, still under emergency threshold. Two-region failover not required.
Mina Shah: Good. Add a note to tenant comms about "expect periodic request queuing and transient tail-latency increases up to 20s for affected cohorts."
Elena Moreno: Draft tenant comms below. Feedback welcome.
```
Maintenance notice: Wed 01:30-03:00 UTC in az4. Impact: brief capacity reduction of az4-gpu-main. We will perform staggered reboots and NIC microcode updates in 4-node cohorts. Some requests may be routed to fallback region or queued briefly. If you require guaranteed reserved capacity during this window, reply with tenant id. Expect transient tail latency and brief increases in error rate during cohort validation.
```
SRE-Liam: Add a line about contacting oncall for urgent SLA concerns. Also include the ops runbook link.
Elena Moreno: Commands for drain step: 
```
kubectl cordon <node>
kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=150 --timeout=10m
```
Theo Briggs: Validation greps: `journalctl -k | grep -i nvlink` and `dmesg | grep -E "MCE|PCIe|link error"` after reboot. Also run `nvidia-smi -q` to check ECC errors.
Mina Shah: Can we pre-warm the backfill pool with low-priority tasks to seed KV caches? That lowers per-token cost.
SRE-Liam: Yes, we'll kick 6 backfill nodes with seed jobs 30m before window.
Elena Moreno: Final items: upload comms to status page, set automated reminder 1h before, and lock the runbook. I'll post the 24h comms tomorrow. Thanks team :thumbsup:
